findings.bug: pagesAvailable = (totalCount / pageSize) + 1 over-reports the page count by one whenever totalCount is an exact multiple of pageSize.
findings.why_real: Correct ceiling division is (totalCount + pageSize - 1) / pageSize. For totalCount=10, pageSize=5 there are exactly 2 pages, but the formula yields 3; the sibling subPageList/calculatePageMetadata never assumes an extra page. The +1 only produces the right answer when totalCount % pageSize != 0.

findings.bug: The byte-stream copy accumulates the copied size in an int (totalBytes) although the method is declared to return long, so counts above 2^31-1 overflow to a negative/wrong value.
findings.why_real: The sibling method copy(Reader,Writer) at line 185 correctly accumulates into a long count. Returning int-widened-to-long means a >2GB stream reports a corrupted size; used by tryDecompress which can produce large outputs.
findings.how_to_prove: Feed copy() a stream longer than Integer.MAX_VALUE bytes -> expected the true byte count, actual an overflowed (possibly negative) value; contrast with the long-based Reader/Writer overload.

findings.bug: append(Object,Object) stores any Object via Hashtable.put, but get() reads with Properties.getProperty, which returns null for any value that is not a String.
findings.why_real: java.util.Properties#getProperty casts only String values ('sval = (oval instanceof String) ? (String)oval : null'). Since append accepts Object value, a non-String value stored via append is silently lost on read.
findings.how_to_prove: new LocalFileMeta().append("k", 123L).get("k") -> expected 123L (or its retrievable value), actual null.

findings.bug: When the last element of the collection is null, a trailing separator is left in the output because the separator is appended for every non-null non-last element regardless of whether any later element is actually emitted.
findings.why_real: The separator is emitted inside 'if (objects[i] != null)' using 'i != size-1', but a trailing null element is skipped entirely, so the separator appended after the preceding element is never followed by content, producing a dangling delimiter.

findings.bug: A group key whose last character is '%' (or has only one char after '%') triggers groupKey.charAt(++i) past the end, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the intended IllegalArgumentException.
findings.why_real: The method is documented to reject malformed keys by throwing IllegalArgumentException('invalid groupkey'), and does so for other malformed cases; a dangling percent escape escapes that contract and surfaces an unrelated exception type.
